title: Best Tidio Alternatives
intro: Tidio's Lyro AI agent reportedly resolves around 90% of conversations with minimal hallucination — a genuinely strong independent signal that earns it a 4/5 AI Quality score in our scorecard — but pricing transparency is the most-repeated complaint across its reviews: roughly 85 of its 1,800+ G2 reviews cite automatic plan upgrades happening without clear permission and friction getting refunds afterward. Channel coverage is the other real limitation — Tidio covers web chat, email, Instagram DM, and Facebook Messenger, with no native WhatsApp, SMS, or voice, and reviewers separately flag a rigid design choice where you can't blend a simple scripted bot with intelligent Lyro handoff in one flow. Both alternatives below carry a disclosure worth noting: this site's author has previously written contributed content for both Chatbase and Crisp, so read these two entries as informed but not neutral, still scored against the same public rubric applied everywhere on this site. Here's what to consider if either of those gaps is the actual dealbreaker for you.

entries.blurb: Chatbase is the closer match on setup speed and pricing tier structure — it shares Tidio's top-tier 5/5 Ease of Setup score in our scorecard, both built around a fast crawl-and-embed workflow, and its entry pricing (Hobby at $32/mo for 700 message credits) lands in a similar range to Tidio's Starter ($24.17/mo, 100 conversations). Where Chatbase pulls ahead of Tidio is channel breadth: voice and telephony unlock at the $120/mo Standard tier, alongside WhatsApp and API access, a real answer to Tidio's channel gap since Tidio has no native WhatsApp or voice at any tier. The trade you're making is AI-quality confidence — Chatbase's AI Quality score in our scorecard is a 3/5, with multiple independent reviews reporting hallucinated answers outside the trained knowledge base, versus Tidio's stronger 4/5 built on that reported ~90% Lyro resolution rate with minimal hallucination. Both platforms share a similar billing quirk, too: Chatbase meters usage in message credits that burn faster on premium models, while Tidio splits its Lyro AI billing into a separate add-on (from $32.50/mo) from the core helpdesk plan — neither is a flat, fully-bundled price. Chatbase's Capterra numbers show the same kind of split reputation Tidio has around billing, just aimed at support instead: a 3.8 customer-service score trailing its 4.6 ease-of-use score. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Chatbase. Worth the swap specifically if you need voice/telephony that Tidio doesn't offer and can tolerate somewhat less AI-quality certainty; stay with Tidio if resolution accuracy is the priority and you don't need those extra channels.

Crisp directly fills Tidio's biggest channel gap — WhatsApp — by bundling it with web chat, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, SMS, and email into one shared inbox from $45/mo (Mini tier), versus Tidio's narrower web/email/Instagram/Messenger lineup. Crisp's AI automation works differently, too: instead of Tidio's separately-billed Lyro add-on (from $32.50/mo for 50+ conversations on top of the core plan), Crisp bundles a dollar-denominated credit pool directly into each tier — $25 of credits, roughly 450 automated conversations, on the $95/mo Essentials plan — which is arguably a cleaner mental model even if the total volume is more modest. On raw AI quality, Tidio still likely has the edge: its 4/5 AI Quality score (built on that ~90% Lyro resolution figure) beats Crisp's 3/5, where one reviewer's cited 40% query-reduction result is real but capped by the same kind of credit-metered budget. Crisp's pricing value actually scores higher in our own comparisons (4/5 versus Tidio's 3/5), reflecting its generous free tier and mid-tier plans sitting well under enterprise competitors, but it carries its own well-documented risk: a 1.9/5 Trustpilot score tied to billing and cancellation complaints that its stronger G2 (4.5/5) and Capterra (4.6/5) numbers don't fully capture. In the interest of full disclosure, this site's author has previously written contributed content for Crisp. Make the swap if WhatsApp coverage is the actual blocker; if AI resolution accuracy is what you value most about Tidio, the Lyro numbers are hard to beat on paper.
